market.category: US journeyman and master electrician NEC exam practice
market.audience: Journeyman and master electrician candidates who need faster open-book lookup and more reliable code calculations before a licensing exam
market.problem: An open-book exam still punishes slow article lookup and skipped calculation steps, while generic question dumps do not show what mistake produced a wrong number
market.advantage: Electrician combines article-navigation drills, five endlessly generated calculation shapes, numbered working, named mistake patterns, and free field tools around the 2023 NEC cycle
market.competitive_context: The category is crowded with small question-bank apps that use a 2026 name, but the open SERP leaves room for a focused practice product that teaches lookup speed and calculation reasoning instead of only repeating a fixed bank

proof_points.claim: The local market research identifies year-suffixed NEC exam searches and an open top SERP for electrician practice apps
The article-match capture makes the open-book lookup task visible as a timed practice decision
The worked-calculation capture shows generated ampacity inputs and four distinct answer traps
The home capture shows short practice, readiness, rooms, field tools, and the 2023 NEC edition in one real product surface

story.throughline: Move from hunting through the NEC to practicing the calculations and traps that decide an open-book exam

frames.header: Find the right NEC article faster

pitch.benefit: Spend the exam finding the rule instead of losing time guessing where it lives
pitch.problem: Open-book questions are still expensive when the candidate cannot identify the article quickly
pitch.advantage: Which Article drills recognition from a situation before the candidate opens the code book
pitch.proof: The literal Which Article screen presents a realistic lookup situation and four article choices

frames.header: Work the numbers step by step

pitch.benefit: Build calculation speed from the order of operations, not from memorizing a fixed answer bank
pitch.problem: A candidate can know the formula and still miss the temperature, conductor-count, or termination step
pitch.advantage: The Five Shapes generates new calculation inputs and keeps the working visible after the answer
pitch.proof: The literal calculation screen shows six current-carrying conductors, ambient temperature, material, terminals, and answer traps

frames.header: Practice the mistakes that cost points

pitch.benefit: Rehearse the judgment calls that turn a technically familiar question into a wrong answer
pitch.problem: Choosing the 90°C column or ignoring the termination cap can look plausible under exam pressure
pitch.advantage: Named mistake patterns turn common wrong choices into targeted follow-up practice
pitch.proof: The literal Ampacity Check screen shows the 90°C versus 75°C termination judgment as a four-choice drill

frames.header: Build a daily code practice habit

pitch.benefit: Turn a few minutes between jobs into repeatable NEC practice
pitch.problem: Long study sessions are hard to start when the next exam or code question is weeks away
pitch.advantage: Quick Session mixes short drills across the covered rooms with visible progress
pitch.proof: The literal Quick Session screen shows a focused ten-question run with a clear prompt and progress

frames.header: See your next practice at a glance

pitch.benefit: Open the app and know whether to start a short session, review readiness, use a room, or check a field tool
pitch.problem: A library of disconnected drills leaves the candidate deciding what to do before practice begins
pitch.advantage: Home puts the next session, readiness signal, rooms, and field tools in one focused lobby
pitch.proof: The literal Home screen shows Quick Session, Practice readiness, Field tools, rooms, and the 2023 NEC edition

frames.header: Keep the code path and tools close

pitch.benefit: Build article fluency in the same app that keeps study calculators ready for field use
pitch.problem: Exam prep usually disappears after the test, while field calculators rarely teach the code path behind the number
pitch.advantage: Code Basics teaches how to navigate the book, and Field Tools states the assumptions behind each estimate
pitch.header_problem: study and field tools split apart
pitch.proof: The literal Code Basics room shows article navigation drills, flashcards, and a direct Which Article practice door
